sam: quick heads-up — saw sustained memory growth on a Qwen-MQA workload during a 1hr long-context replay. KV map size keeps creeping even after sequences end.
jess: ugh. is this the same trace as the rope-scaling run from yesterday?
sam: related but different input distribution. repro: long chats with repeated role tokens + system prefix churn. growth starts ~50k steps.
carla: can you paste the heap map snapshot?
sam: pasted below (trimmed):
```
KV map entries: 3.2M -> 3.8M over 45m
Allocated pages: 18,432 -> 20,110
Fragmentation ratio: 0.28 -> 0.35
Paged-out segments: 0 -> 12
Eviction passes: 4 (no high-confidence evictions)
Model: qwen-7b-mqa, rope scaling: enabled, kv-slot-size: 64
```
omar: interesting that paged-out segments appear only after fragmentation hits ~0.3. looks like the pager triggers but doesn't compact, just marks pages.
sam: exact. below is the profiler snippet where reuse drops:
```
perf: kv_reuse_rate 0.72 -> 0.48
perf: avg_lookup_latency +12%
hotspot: slot_allocator->lookup_slow_path 92%
```
jess: MQA could be causing non-uniform slot sizes when we merge heads, so free lists get skewed. does the same trace with Llama-MQA behave similarly?
sam: tried llama-13b-mqa — less growth, fragmentation stable ~0.15. Mistral-8B shows weird spikes when rope tokens oscillate.
carla: so qwen-specific quirk? maybe its key lengths or the way attention is sharded. can you capture raw KV index distribution?
sam: attached bucket histogram (small sample):
```
bucket 0-64: 22%
64-128: 49%
128-256: 19%
256+: 10%
skew metric: 0.62
```
omar: that 64-128 spike aligns with our slot-granularity mismatch. if slot size=64 but MQA merge writes variable-length segments, we might be leaving tail fragments.
carla: evictions look non-aggressive — policy uses LRU with time-based grace for long contexts. maybe too conservative. could force compaction on pager heartbeat when fragmentation > 0.25.
infra-bot: deploy bot: rolled a canary with pager-compact tweak to eng-runtime-canary at 1851234500.
jess: nice. any perf hits? compaction can be expensive if we do it mid-peak.
sam: canary results: memory stabilized, fragmentation down to 0.18, but p99 latency +7ms during compaction windows. throughput unaffected.
omar: tradeoff seems reasonable for long-tail sessions. maybe make compaction adaptive: only run if fragmentation > threshold and current concurrency < X.
carla: also consider kernel selection: switch to the compacting allocator kernel for Qwen runs only. we have a cheaper fast-path that avoids compaction but it assumes uniform segment sizes.
jess: good call. add a routing rule: if model contains "qwen" && batching profile == long-context, route to compacting kernel.
sam: agree. I'll open a small RFC with telemetry changes to capture slot skew, reuse_rate, and compaction-time.
carla: add a regression test: synthetic replay with alternating long and short prefixes + repeated role tokens. assert fragmentation < 0.22 after 1h.
omar: and add a metric for "pager_compactions" and "compaction_latency_ms". we'll alert if compactions spike without fragmentation improvement.
sam: action items: 1) RFC + telemetry (sam), 2) adaptive compaction policy (omar), 3) kernel routing rule for qwen long-context (carla), 4) regression test + canary (jess).
carla: I'll prototype allocator kernel switch tomorrow.
infra-bot: incident bot: created ticket INF-8723 for the Qwen KV fragmentation investigation.
sam: thanks all — will post perf graphs in #eng-runtime once RFC lands. :thumbsup:
